skill.displayName: Pet Body Condition Score 3D Analysis | 宠物体态3D评分（BCS）

llm.summary: The skill appears to perform the advertised pet body-score analysis, but it also silently creates or reuses an account identity, sends identity data to a remote service, and stores access tokens locally.

dimensions.detail: Reading user-supplied media and sending it to analysis APIs is expected, but reading workspace identity material from data/smyx-api-key.txt and binding requests to a locally persisted identity is not clearly scoped to user-selected inputs.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No separate installer or manifest was found; the artifact is a skill directory with Python scripts and requirements, but it does not clearly declare the runtime capabilities it depends on, including network access, local media reads, local database writes, and shell-invoked scripts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions explicitly tell the agent not to ask for or reveal internal identity values while using them for analysis and history lookup, which materially reduces user visibility and control over account-scoped behavior.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The code creates or updates a workspace SQLite database and can store user profile fields plus token and open_token values for reuse; this persistent credential/session behavior is high impact and under-disclosed.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Server-side pet media analysis and cloud history lookup match the stated purpose, but the shared runtime also performs silent identity provisioning, login/registration, token handling, and profile persistence that are broader than simple BCS scoring.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with this skill sending pet media or supplied URLs to lifeemergence.com services, automatically creating or reusing an internal account identity, querying cloud history, and storing reusable authentication tokens in a local workspace database. Avoid using it with sensitive household footage unless you understand the service's retention and account controls.
llm.findings:
[AST7] unexpected: Dynamic ORM filtering is present in shared DAO list/count helpers, but I did not find a direct user-controlled path from this skill's documented CLI flow to those filter dictionaries.
[LP3] unexpected: The runtime capabilities are real and broader than the metadata expresses; this supports a transparency concern, not an automatic malicious finding.
[SDI-1] expected: Cloud history report listing is explicitly documented in SKILL.md and implemented by the --list path, so that part is not hidden, though it depends on account-scoped data access.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Silent identity resolution, remote login/registration, and local token/profile persistence are broader than the core BCS analysis task and are not presented as user-controlled configuration.
[SQP-2] expected: Uploading local media or forwarding URLs to a server is central to the advertised analysis and is disclosed, but the artifact gives limited user-facing detail about destination, retention, and confirmation.
[E1] unexpected: External analysis requests are expected, but the additional phoneLogin request sends identity fields and can register an account silently, which is the main Review concern.
